questions.question_text: Of all reported parasomnias, the one that is more common in females than males is
questions.explanation: Women report nightmares more frequently, in a ratio of 2 -4:1. Among children, sleep terror disorder is more prevalent in males than in females, but in adults, the ratio is even. REM sleep behaviour disorder is more prevalent in males. Sleepwalking disorder and restless leg syndrome have an equal sex distribution.

questions.question_text: On corneal examination, Kayser -Fleischer rings are usually present in patients with
questions.explanation: Wilson's disease: Personality disturbances, mood abnormalities, and cognitive dysfunction being the most common psychiatric symptoms. Kayser -Fleischer rings (copper deposits on Descemet's membrane of the cornea) are present in 95% of patients with neurological symptoms, in 50 -60% of patients without neurological symptoms and in only 10% of asymptomatic siblings. 50% of patients will have mental disturbances at some point during the course of the disease.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is preserved in apperceptive visual agnosia?
questions.explanation: Visual agnosia refers to defective recognition of stimulus presented visually despite the intact sensory system. Lissauer classified this into 1. Apperceptive visual agnosia and 2. Associative visual agnosia on the basis of a two-stage model of recognition. In the former, the patient never achieves a complete visual percept while, in the latter, such percept is formed but could not be associated with its semantic meaning. Hence in apperceptive agnosia, drawing of objects, writing one's name and copying diagrams are preserved.

questions.question_text: Which of the following tremors increase during intentional movement?
questions.explanation: Tremors triggered or made worse by movement are called action tremors. Action tremors can be classified as intention tremors (triggered by aiming for a target) or postural tremors (triggered by holding a limb in one position). Most parkinsonian tremors are resting tremors: they are less pronounced on initiating movement.

questions.question_text: A 76-year-old man was brought to the emergency unit by his wife. He had breakfast that morning and appeared unable to remember that he and his wife have planned a day out. He repeatedly enquired where she was taking him. She reports that he appeared bewildered, but was alert and had no sensory and motor deficits throughout. He returned to a normal mental state after 10 hours. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Transient global amnesia (TGA) refers to an episode of complete and reversible anterograde and retrograde memory loss lasting up to 24 h. Patients have a persistent loss of memory for the time of the attack. During the episode, patients often appear bewildered and ask repeated questions.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drugs is contraindicated in angle closure glaucoma?
questions.explanation: Topiramate can increase intraocular pressure and can cause acute precipitation of angle closure glaucoma.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drugs has the best available evidence for the treatment of depression that follows a myocardial infarction?
questions.explanation: The Sertraline Antidepressant Heart Attack Randomized Trial (SADHART) is to date the largest randomized trial evaluating use of antidepressant medication for depressed patients with heart disease.

questions.question_text: What is the risk of depression in a cardiac patient with congestive heart failure compared to the general population?
questions.explanation: The prevalence rates of clinically significant depression among CHF patients is approximately 21.5%, determined using meta -analytic tests.

questions.question_text: The mean age of onset of chronic fatigue syndrome is between
questions.explanation: The mean age of onset is between 29 -35 years.

questions.question_text: The ratio of prevalence of Chronic Fatigue Syndrome in males compared to females is
questions.explanation: The prevalence of Chronic Fatigue Syndrome is nearly 0.5% with a higher rate in women [M -F - 1:3], those belonging to lower occupational status and educational background.

questions.question_text: Diagnostic features of neurasthenia include the following except:
questions.explanation: The diagnostic criteria for neurasthenia are: a. either, persistent and distressing feelings of exhaustion after minor mental effort or persistent and distressing feelings of fatigue after minor physical effort; b. accompanied by one or more of the following symptoms: muscular aches or pains; dizziness; tension headache; sleep disturbance; inability to relax; and irritability; c. inability to recover through rest, relaxation or enjoyment; d. duration exceeds 3 months; e. Does not occur in the presence of organic mental disorders, affective disorders or panic or generalized anxiety disorder.

questions.question_text: A 42 -year-old woman presents with a history of 2 episodes of unilateral blindness that lasted for few weeks. Now she has paraesthesia of left leg and MRI shows multiple demyelinating plaques. Which of the following with regard to her illness is correct?

options.text: It presents with diverse physical signs
It is more common in men than women
It is due to a bacterial infection
It has a uniform progressive course.
Occurs more commonly nearer the equator

correct_answer.text: It presents with diverse physical signs

correct_answers.text: It presents with diverse physical signs

questions.explanation: The description is suggestive of multiple sclerosis. In the UK, the lifetime risk is 1:8000; It is twice as common in women as in men and is seen with greater frequency as the distance from the equator increases.

questions.question_text: Which of the following symptoms are not indicative of chronic fatigue syndrome?
questions.explanation: The core symptom of CFS is fatigue. However, pain and cognitive difficulties can be as prominent as fatigue. According to NICE, symptoms that might indicate another serious illness include significant weight loss; clinically significant lymphadenopathy; localising or focal neurological signs; features of inflammatory arthritis, connective tissue disease, or cardiorespiratory disease; and sleep apnoea.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a feature of sleep terror disorder?

options.text: Vivid memory of dreams on waking up

questions.explanation: The average sleep terror episode lasts for about 15 minutes. Sleep terror is an NREM disorder - unlike nightmares, the memory of the dream or even of arousal is poor on waking up. An increase in muscle tone with two to four -fold increase in heart rate is observed.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is an example of subcortical dementia?
questions.explanation: Sub cortical dementias include Parkinson's disease dementia, Huntington's disease, HIV -associated dementia, Binswanger's disease and Wilson's disease. Subcortical dementias are characterised by gross psychomotor slowing, abnormal movements, low mood, mild amnesia and apathetic personality.

questions.question_text: A 33 -year-old woman has been referred by the dentist with a long history of facial tingling, numbness, nausea and temperomandibular joint pain. The pain tends to fluctuate and they were anatomically inconsistent. Further investigations have shown no abnormality. The most likely diagnosis would be;
questions.explanation: Somatoform disorder: This condition is characterised by patients with chronic pain that is not caused by any physical or specific psychiatric symptoms.

questions.question_text: A cognitive faculty most often affected in patients with post concussion syndrome is
questions.explanation: Processing speed is the most affected - correlates with severity of symptoms.

questions.question_text: Which of the following symptoms occur commonly in patients with postconcussional syndrome?

options.text: Short term memory loss and personality changes
Dizziness, headaches, irritability, slowed mental process

correct_answer.text: Dizziness, headaches, irritability, slowed mental process

correct_answers.text: Dizziness, headaches, irritability, slowed mental process

questions.explanation: Post concussional syndrome is the commonest psychiatric disorder following head injury. It occurs following head trauma, usually sufficiently severe to result in loss of consciousness.

questions.question_text: A patient had a stroke 8 months ago. He now presents with apathy, amotivation and anhedonia. He does not have any tearfulness or pessimism. His MMSE score is 22/30 and he has dysexecutive function. What is his most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Patients who have vascular depression have more apathy, retardation, less depressive thinking such as guilt and worthlessness, poor executive function on cognitive testing, than do elderly individuals who are depressed without vascular risk factors.

questions.question_text: A 29 -year-old woman, who is 6 months pregnant, is referred to your clinic for an opinion. She is depressed, has a previous history of depression and a family history of depression. She has responded well to paroxetine in the past. If she were to continue with Paroxetine throughout pregnancy, which of the following effects is most likely to be seen in the newborn?
questions.explanation: Paroxetine, particularly high -dose first trimesters exposure, is clearly linked to cardiac malformation - VSD and ASD.

questions.question_text: An antidepressant with best evidence for use in post stroke depression is
questions.explanation: Nortriptyline is a second-generation tricyclic antidepressant. Patients with cardiovascular disease should be given nortriptyline only under close supervision because of the tendency of the drug to produce tachycardia and to prolong the conduction time (QT) like most other tricyclics.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pregnant mothers have the highest risk of having a child with ADHD?

options.text: 22 year old lady who smokes one joint of marijuana a day
31 year old lady who drinks 3 mugs of coffee a day
26 year old lady who has no substance use habits
30 year old lady who drinks one glass of red wine a day
21 year old lady who smokes 12 'roll -up' cigarettes a day

correct_answer.text: 21 year old lady who smokes 12 'roll -up' cigarettes a day

correct_answers.text: 21 year old lady who smokes 12 'roll -up' cigarettes a day

questions.explanation: Nicotine exposure in pregnancy is increasingly being associated with the risk of ADHD in children.

questions.question_text: A 21 -year-old woman has been diagnosed with postnatal depression and is currently receiving antidepressant treatment. Which observer rating would be most appropriate to use, to assess her response to treatment?
questions.explanation: Montgomery Asberg depression rating scale (MADRS) is a 10 items version, which is most sensitive to change when measuring the severity of depression.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is correct with regard to the mechanism of action of modafinil?
questions.explanation: Modafinil's exact mechanism of action is still not known, but it exhibits selectivity for hypothalamic arousal systems and has been shown to activate orexin neurons in rodents.

questions.question_text: Modafinil, which is used for daytime sleepiness, causes which of the following neurochemical changes?
questions.explanation: Modafinil, like other stimulants, increases the release of monoamines specifically the catecholamines, norepinephrine and dopamine from the synaptic terminals.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a common side effect of modafinil?
questions.explanation: Modafinil has side effects that include headache, appetite suppression, nervousness, and sleep disturbance.

questions.question_text: Which of the following antidepressants has an effect in common with anti -nausea drugs such as ondansetron?
questions.explanation: Mirtazapine can block 5HT3 receptors similar to the anti -nausea drugs ondansetron used in cancer chemotherapy.

questions.question_text: A 30 -year-old woman with a history of bipolar disorder is currently breastfeeding her child. She has a manic relapse, though the presentation is not severe enough to warrant hospitalisation. What would be the best medication to treat her relapse?
questions.explanation: If necessary one may use valproate. Treatment of bipolar disorder invariably requires mood stabilizers.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a characteristic symptom of hepatic encephalopathy?
questions.explanation: Liver flap is seen in hepatic failure associated with encephalopathic state.

questions.question_text: A 45 -year-old woman comes to see you with her husband. He is concerned about her behaviour - she seems on a constant high and has spent a lot of their money on shopping sprees. She is completely unconcerned about that but is worried about a rash on her face and tells you that she has had several mouth ulcers recently. The rash on her face gets worse on sunny days. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: It is important to note that SLE can present as camouflaged bipolar disorder.

questions.question_text: Which of the following modes of psychotherapy has established evidence in HIV associated depression?
questions.explanation: Interpersonal therapy has established evidence in HIV related depression.

questions.question_text: A man presents with drooping of the left lip and inability to fully close his left eye though he can frown. What is the likely cause of the lesion?

options.text: Facial nerve palsy(lower motor neuron type)
Facial nerve palsy (upper motor neuron type)

correct_answer.text: Facial nerve palsy (upper motor neuron type)

correct_answers.text: Facial nerve palsy (upper motor neuron type)

questions.explanation: In UMN palsy of facial nerve, the upper part of face is spared.

questions.question_text: In which of the following neurological conditions anaemia is a common finding?
questions.explanation: In subacute combined degeneration of cord (SACD), vitamin B12 deficiency produces spinal degeneration, peripheral neuropathy and macrocytic anaemia.

questions.question_text: The prevalence of comorbid depression in those with coronary heart disease is
questions.explanation: In patients with CHD, the prevalence of major depression is nearly 20%, and the prevalence of a minor depressive disorder is approximately 27%.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about suicide rates in patients with Huntington's disease?
questions.explanation: In Huntington's disease, the risk of suicide is 4 times higher than the general population.

questions.question_text: Amnesia is the most common residual deficit following recovery from
questions.explanation: Herpes simplex encephalitis affects temporal lobes resulting in residual amnesia that may persist after recovery from the acute infection.

questions.question_text: Which of the following occurs in Ganser's syndrome?

options.text: Disorientation in time, place and person

questions.explanation: Ganser's syndrome is a rare syndrome characterized by approximate answers, clouded consciousness, pseudo-hallucinations and hysterical conversion symptoms.

questions.question_text: A patient known to have bipolar disorder with mixed affective state is in the first trimester of her pregnancy. She has not been on any medications of late. What would you prescribe to her?
questions.explanation: For women who have had a long period without relapse, the possibilities of withdrawing treatment before conception and for a least the first trimester should be considered.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following medications could be used to treat pathological crying?
questions.explanation: For pathological crying, fluoxetine and sertraline have been evaluated in small parallel RCTs with favourable results.

questions.question_text: A pregnant bipolar patient has no other treatment option but to continue valproate. Which of the following should she take in addition?
questions.explanation: Folate supplements reduce the risk of neural tube defects.

questions.question_text: What would be the most appropriate drug for a depressed lady who is pregnant?
questions.explanation: Fluoxetine has the most evidence and is safer than paroxetine.

questions.question_text: Which of the following points towards dissociative pseudoseizures rather than epileptic seizures?

options.text: Total duration being less than 30 secs

questions.explanation: Features which are common in pseudoseizures but rarer in epilepsy include: biting the tip of the tongue, seizures lasting more than 2 minutes, seizures having a gradual onset, a fluctuating course of disease severity, the eyes being closed during a seizure, and side to side head movements.

questions.question_text: Idiopathic progressive calcium deposition in the basal ganglia is seen in
questions.explanation: Fahr's disease is caused due to idiopathic progressive calcium deposition in the basal ganglia.

questions.question_text: Presence of which of the following will prompt investigations for a medical cause of recurrent anxiety?

options.text: Onset of symptoms before the age of 25 years

questions.explanation: Factors that imply an organic aetiology for anxiety include - onset of symptoms after the age of 35 years, lack of anticipatory anxiety, lack of avoidance behavior, and lack of personal or family history of anxiety disorders and poor response to short term anxiolytics.

questions.question_text: What percentage of women with postpartum psychosis will go on to develop schizophrenia later in their lifetime?
questions.explanation: Diagnostically, most patients with postpartum psychosis later receive a diagnosis of affective disorder; schizophrenia is diagnosed in around 16%.

questions.question_text: Which of the following symptoms do you see more often in the later rather than the early stages of HIV dementia?
questions.explanation: Except paraparesis, other symptoms are seen even in early stages of HIV dementia.

questions.question_text: Most common psychiatric symptom in Cushing's syndrome is
questions.explanation: Cushing's syndrome, the result of an excess of corticosteroid, is very frequently, although not invariably, associated with depression.

questions.question_text: Which of the following MRI finding is characteristically seen in Huntington's disease?
questions.explanation: Caudate atrophy with box-car ventricles is noted in Huntington's.

questions.question_text: Mr. Y has been treated for multiple sclerosis, and he developed depression following treatment. Which of the following drugs is most likely to have induced the depression?
questions.explanation: Beta and alpha interferons used in the treatment of multiple sclerosis is associated with depression.

questions.question_text: A 45 -year-old diabetic gentleman was brought to the emergency department with nausea, vomiting, lethargy and muscle cramps. He has been diagnosed with depression and has been started on fluoxetine recently. What is the most likely metabolic complication?
questions.explanation: All antidepressants can cause hyponatremia, especially SSRIs like Fluoxetine.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an effective treatment for post-stroke depression based on the best available evidence?
questions.explanation: A meta-analysis that pooled 385 patients from 6 trials published through December 2009 that evaluated the prophylactic efficacy of fluoxetine in poststroke patients. They found that fluoxetine reduced the incidence of poststroke depression, helped recovery in neurologic function, and improved independence in activities of daily living.

questions.question_text: What rating scale would you recommend to a health visitor who wants to screen for depression in women after delivery?
questions.explanation: EPDS is a 10 -item self -report scale to screen for Postnatal Depression in the community. The scale can be completed in about 5 minutes and has a simple method of scoring that can be used by health visitors and midwives.

questions.question_text: In ICD 10 which of the following is included under dissociative disorders?
questions.explanation: 'Trance and possession' disorders are placed under the general rubric of dissociative disorder (ICD -10) implying a psychological causation of symptoms.

questions.question_text: What is the case fatality rate in patients with herpes simplex encephalitis?
questions.explanation: Untreated, there is a case fatality of ~70% for Herpes simplex encephalitis. Treatment with intravenous aciclovir reduces fatality to 20 -30%.

questions.question_text: During the psychiatric consultation, Mr. Y says 'I feel like a woman trapped in a man's body'. This describes a core clinical feature seen in
questions.explanation: Transsexualism is characterized by the feeling of one's gender being different from one's biological sex. These patients have an enduring belief that they are really of the opposite sex.

questions.question_text: A 33 year old man has intractable seizures. Which of the following factors may support a diagnosis of non-epileptic seizures rather than true epilepsy?

options.text: Less likely to maintain body tone during a seizure
More likely to sustain injury from seizures

questions.explanation: The following factors in the history may support a diagnosis of non-epileptic seizures. Regaining alertness and orientation rapidly, Ability to recall events clearly, The presence of social stressors.

questions.question_text: As regards drug therapy in palliative care all are true except

options.text: Risperidone may be useful for psychotic symptoms in terminally ill patients
Tricyclics may produce troublesome side effects and delirium.
Lorazepam is useful for acute anxiety
Amitryptyline is useful for neuropathic pain
SSRIs have well established evidence base for depression in palliative care

correct_answer.text: SSRIs have well established evidence base for depression in palliative care

correct_answers.text: SSRIs have well established evidence base for depression in palliative care

questions.explanation: The evidence base for treating various psychiatric symptoms in palliative care is feeble; the use of SSRIs is empirical rather than evidence-based.

questions.question_text: MRI shows hypointensity of striatum in patients with
questions.explanation: The commonest neurological features of FD are Parkinsonism, chorea, dystonia, tremor, gait disturbance, dysarthria, seizures, and myoclonus.

questions.question_text: 'Baby blues' are reported in what proportion of new mothers?
questions.explanation: Baby blues: Up to 3/4 of new mothers will experience a short-lived period of tearfulness and emotional lability starting two or three days after birth and lasting one or two days.

questions.question_text: Doctor-shopping is an entity associated with which psychiatric condition?
questions.explanation: Somatisation disorder: Diagnosis is usually only suspected after negative findings begin to emerge as normal medical practice is to take complaints at face value.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is incorrect about somatisation disorder?

options.text: Usually have long complex medical histories
Most frequent symptoms are non-specific and atypical
It is associated with significant psychological distress and functional impairment
Symptoms are usually localised to a single physiological system
Usually presents before the age of 40

correct_answer.text: Symptoms are usually localised to a single physiological system

correct_answers.text: Symptoms are usually localised to a single physiological system

questions.explanation: Somatisation disorder is a chronic disorder of multiple medically unexplained symptoms, affecting multiple organ systems presenting before the age of 40.

questions.question_text: What percentage of patients will die by completed suicide in the 12 months after an initial parasuicidal act?
questions.explanation: Risk of suicide within one year of DSH - 0.7% (nearly 1 in 100); more in males 1.1%; 0.5% in females.

questions.question_text: The risk factors for completed suicide would include all except
questions.explanation: Risk factors for completed suicide Socio-demographic factors: Male sex, Elderly, Single, divorced, or widowed.

questions.question_text: Presentations featured by 'episodic panic attacks' are reported most often in patients with;
questions.explanation: Pheochromocytoma: Catecholamine-secreting tumour. Physically - tachycardia, labile hypertension, headache, sweating, and palpitations - episodic.

questions.question_text: The peak incidence of head injury is between the ages of
questions.explanation: Peak incidence of head injury is between the ages of 15 - 24 years.

questions.question_text: The most common co-morbid psychiatric condition associated with hypochondriasis is
questions.explanation: Patients with hypochondriasis have a high rate of psychiatric comorbidity.

questions.question_text: Which lobe of the brain is commonly affected in patients with herpes simplex encephalitis?
questions.explanation: In children older than 3 months and in adults, HSE is usually localized to the temporal and frontal lobes.

questions.question_text: Mrs. P suffers from epilepsy and clinical depression. She has been tried on SSRIs with no benefit and is keen to try older antidepressants. The safest choice in her case would be;
questions.explanation: Moclobemide is not known to be pro-convulsive and is a good choice.

questions.question_text: Which one among the following is not an observation normally associated with Herpes simplex encephalitis?

options.text: Gold standard for in vivo diagnosis is CSF polymerase chain reaction (PCR) for herpes viruses.
CT Scan usually reveals signal change and swelling within the frontal lobes
The EEG is invariably abnormal in HSE.
Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) examination commonly reveals a lymphocytosis and a raised protein
Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the imaging of choice in HSE

correct_answer.text: CT Scan usually reveals signal change and swelling within the frontal lobes

correct_answers.text: CT Scan usually reveals signal change and swelling within the frontal lobes

questions.explanation: Neuroimaging usually reveals signal change and swelling within the temporal lobes.

questions.question_text: Most cases of herpes simplex encephalitis are caused by
questions.explanation: In children older than 3 months and in adults, HSE is usually localized to the temporal and frontal lobes and is caused by herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1).
